aula.titulo: The imperative with pronouns and instructions
aula.objetivo: Use the affirmative and negative imperative with pronouns («donne-le-moi», «ne le fais pas»), and give instructions, recipes and rules.

blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: in the AFFIRMATIVE imperative, the pronoun comes AFTER the verb, joined by a hyphen: «Regarde-le !» «Écoute-moi !» «Donne-lui le livre.» STEP 2: «me» and «te» become «moi» and «toi» at the end: «Écoute-moi.» «Lève-toi.» STEP 3: with two pronouns, the direct one comes first: «Donne-le-moi.» «Dis-le-lui.» «Envoie-les-nous.» STEP 4: in the NEGATIVE imperative, the pronoun goes back BEFORE the verb, as in the present tense: «Ne le regarde pas !» «Ne me dis pas ça !» «Ne le lui donne pas !» STEP 5: «y» and «en» also come after the verb in the affirmative, and the verb takes an «s» when it ends in «e»: «Vas-y !» «Prends-en !» «Manges-en !» STEP 6: with reflexive verbs: «Lève-toi !» «Assieds-toi !» «Dépêchez-vous !» STEP 7: negative reflexive: «Ne te lève pas !» «Ne vous dépêchez pas !» STEP 8: the imperative is formed from «tu», «nous» and «vous»: «Mange !» «Mangeons !» «Mangez !» (the «s» of «tu» drops from «-er» verbs, except before «y» and «en»).
blocos.comparacao: In English the pronoun always comes after the verb («give me», «give him», «don't give me»). French does that only in the affirmative («donne-moi»); in the negative the pronoun goes before the verb («ne me donne pas»). Also note the hyphen and the change «me → moi».

erros.motivo: In the affirmative, the pronoun comes after.
In the negative, it comes before the verb.

blocos.enunciado: Give ten commands out loud: five affirmative and five negative, with pronouns.
Write and say out loud a short email confirming a meeting.
